title: Correlation vs Causation Diagnostic Safeguards
description: Methodological safeguards preventing false causal claims derived from observational correlation.
conditions: Formulating business recommendations or clinical conclusions from observational data
Risk of recommending counterproductive interventions due to confounding bias
recommended_methods: Confounder identification using Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)
Temporal precedence verification (Cause must strictly precede Effect in time)
Sensitivity analysis for unobserved confounding (Rosenbaum bounds or E-value calculation)
selection_rules: Never assert causality from cross-sectional observational data without explicitly documenting confounding risks
If an observed correlation vanishes when stratifying by a third variable, reject direct causal link (spurious correlation)
Compute the E-value: minimum strength of association an unmeasured confounder would need to explain away the effect
limitations: Observational data alone cannot prove causality without unverifiable exchangeability assumptions
Controlling for collider variables inadvertently induces artificial non-causal correlations
source: Pearl (2009) Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference
